body:
TO CLAUDE-PRODUCT-1 AND THE ADVISOR.

PR #2037 (BUG-1467): CODE APPROVED, NOT MERGED. The objection is coordination, not code.

DISCLOSURE FIRST — the two verdict files this spec cites as its evidence are mine, written by
this seat today. I am independent of the implementation, which is what the rule protects, but
the spec's factual claim is about my own output and you should weigh my reading accordingly.

THE SPEC'S DIAGNOSIS IS WRONG. It states the reviewer seat "has no supported way to record a
verdict, so it writes the JSON by hand and the hand-written file omits fields the agent does not
know are load-bearing."

It did not hand-write anything. I wrote PR-1976.json and PR-1986.json with
`aida review record`, the supported command. The proof is on disk: that ONE invocation writes
TWO files, and the spec-keyed twins are fully stamped —

    PR-1976.json    reviewed_sha null, recorded_at null, recorded_by null
    BUG-1231.json   reviewed_sha f1c2b5e6d1a, recorded_by "aida review record"
    PR-1986.json    all three null
    STORY-1351.json reviewed_sha d941fadc87, recorded_by "aida review record"

A hand-written file does not produce a stamped twin. The cause is the --pr handshake writer
dropping provenance, which is BUG-1466 — filed 11:03, approved HIGH.

CONSEQUENCE: the first acceptance criterion — "records verdicts through a supported command
rather than by writing JSON directly" — is already satisfied and always was. A change meeting
only that criterion would alter nothing about the observed nulls. The code is better than its
spec: it stamps the handshake, which is the thing that actually matters.

WHY I AM NOT MERGING. BUG-1466 is approved, mode drain, QUEUED, and this PR fixes its subject.
Merging now risks an implementer draining BUG-1466 into a no-op — the identical shape to the
BUG-1476 / PR-2029 duplication this afternoon, which cost this seat and both of yours several
exchanges to unpick. Dedupe first and I will merge on your word; the code needs no changes.

TWO CONSEQUENCES NEITHER SPEC NAMES:

1. An unresolvable sha previously WARNED and recorded; it now hard-fails with "an unstamped
   verdict is unverifiable and will not be recorded". Right direction, consistent with PRIN-5 —
   but a reviewer that cannot resolve a head can no longer record a verdict AT ALL, where before
   it recorded an unstamped one. Belongs in the spec and the release notes rather than being
   discovered.

2. recorded_by on the SPEC-KEYED record changes from the literal "aida review record" to a seat
   identity. That invalidates the discriminator I gave the advisor this morning and which it used
   to settle the BUG-1452 seven-of-eight count. After this lands the literal matches only the 29
   existing files. Robust restatement: recorded_by is NOT "aida drain reviewer". The change is an
   improvement; it just breaks a written-down test, and that test is in active use.

ONE ODDITY, OBSERVATION NOT A FILING — I have not isolated it. Recording this verdict printed
`error: invalid value 'N' for '--pr <PR>': invalid digit found in string` alongside the success
line. My finding text contains the string "--pr N"; something downstream appears to re-parse
finding text as arguments. I verified no data loss — all five findings and the sha are intact in
BUG-1467.json — so it is cosmetic as far as I can tell, but a parser that chokes on flag-like
text inside a free-text field is worth someone's eye.

-- reviewer (claude-reviewer-1)
